## Overview

Run GLM-5.3-Flash's MoE layers with DeepGEMM's FP8xFP8 MegaMoE (routed and shared experts in one kernel that also dispatches and combines across the EP group), using the official FP8 checkpoint. Enabled by `--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'` with `--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size N --enable-expert-parallel`.

Related: #55275 (BF16 / MXFP4 MegaMoE for GLM, open), #54049 (FlashInfer NVFP4 mega kernel).

## Claims

- On the AgentX replay at concurrency 96, DEP4 with MegaMoE gives 1.6x the output throughput of DEP4 on the generic MoE path.
- Against TP4 it is about level on throughput (+6%, one run each) and has about a fifth of the TTFT.
- It prefills 1.8x faster than DEP4 generic and 2.5x faster than TP4.
- AIME 2026 Pass@1 matches the generic MoE path (0.934 vs 0.939 with a 131K output cap) and is 0.977 with the 1M context.
- A weight reload, in layerwise or direct mode, restores byte-identical weights at the same addresses.
- No change for any other `moe_backend`.

## Validation

4x B200, nightly `8cbd5d03` with this change applied, MTP 5 with acceptance fixed by `synthetic_acceptance_length` 3.61. The three arms ran on the same node and in the same container, one run each; they differ only in parallel layout and `moe_backend`.

AgentX replay (InferenceX-pinned aiperf, `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126`), concurrency 96, 1 hour:

| metric | TP4 | DEP4, generic MoE | DEP4, MegaMoE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| output tok/s | 3,152 | 2,063 | **3,332** |
| input tok/s | 380,126 | 234,727 | **399,297** |
| total tok/s | 383,278 | 236,790 | **402,628** |
| requests completed (errors) | 11,372 (4) | 8,143 (1) | 11,986 (5) |
| TTFT avg / p50 / p99 | 3.93 / 2.19 / 23.8 s | 2.36 / 1.47 / 17.3 s | **0.81 / 0.49 / 5.99 s** |
| ITL avg | 18.3 ms | 45.6 ms | 19.5 ms |
| output tok/s per user | 64.0 | 26.2 | 64.1 |
| prefix cache hit | 93.9% | 92.4% | 94.0% |
| of which GPU / host reload | 6.2% / 87.7% | 50.9% / 41.5% | 71.2% / 22.8% |
| preemptions | 35 | 53 | 2 |

`vllm bench serve`, random prompts, concurrency 128, on the same servers:

| workload (in/out) | metric | TP4 | DEP4, generic MoE | DEP4, MegaMoE |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 / 1 | total tok/s | 46,334 | 63,900 | **115,081** |
| | mean TTFT | 20.8 s | 15.2 s | 8.4 s |
| 1024 / 1024 | output tok/s | 7,895 | 8,478 | **11,691** |
| | mean TTFT | 4.31 s | 1.86 s | 0.85 s |

Accuracy:

| eval | TP4 | DEP4, generic MoE | DEP4, MegaMoE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K, lm-eval 5-shot, 1,319 questions | 0.9757 ± 0.0042 | – | 0.9735 ± 0.0044 |
| AIME 2026 Pass@1, 30 problems x 32 samples | – | 0.939 ± 0.006 | 0.934 ± 0.006 |

GSM8K ran on nightly `43b4aaea` (TP4) and the servers above (MegaMoE). AIME ran on nightly `df3bd094` with this branch, both arms in the same container (MTP 3, fp8 KV, 131K output cap) with DeepInfer's `eval/aime` prompt and rule-based judge, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95; the generic arm runs `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` on the checkpoint's own scales. With the full 1M context MegaMoE reaches **0.977 ± 0.005**; the remaining loss is mostly problem 15 (0.72), where 12 of 32 samples never stop and loop until the context is full.

Weight reload, 4x B200, nightly `e0d00e4b8e` with this branch, DEP4, MTP 3. The experts are zeroed before each reload, which breaks every greedy output; all results are compared with the cold start:

| metric | layerwise | direct |
|---|---:|---:|
| target reload time | 41.6 s | 37.3 s |
| parameters and buffers differing (5,900 across ranks) | 0 | 0 |
| parameters and buffers moved | 0 | 0 |
| greedy outputs matching (4 short prompts) | 4/4 | 4/4 |

The same holds for a second reload, a reload of the MTP drafter, and an update that sends expert weights and block scales in separate `load_weights` calls. Long prompts (about 14K tokens) already vary between identical runs without a reload, on both MoE backends, so they are not compared. No real NCCL or IPC trainer was run.

Unit tests: `pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_mega_moe.py`, 5 passed.

```bash
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 8190 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 \
  --prefix-match-unit 16 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":300000000000,"enable_cross_layers_blocks":"true","lazy_offload":false}}'

aiperf profile --scenario agentx --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --concurrency 96 --benchmark-duration 3600 \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126
```

AIME 2026:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92
```

The client sends DeepInfer's `eval/aime` prompts (`build_records`) to `/v1/chat/completions` with `temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95`, 32 samples per problem, and scores `reasoning + "</think>" + content` with its `score_rollout`. Samples were drawn with a 131K output cap first; the 82 that hit it were continued from their own text to the 1M context, which samples the same distribution as the larger cap.

The baselines drop `moe_backend` (DEP4, generic) or use `--tensor-parallel-size 4` alone with `--intra-node-data-parallel-size 1` on the router (TP4). The generic path picked `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` for the FP8 experts. The random-prompt rows were measured on the same servers before the replay with `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --max-concurrency 128`.
</details>

## Details

- The checkpoint's experts are block FP8 (E4M3, one float32 scale per 128x128 block). DeepGEMM's SM100 MegaMoE feeds scales to the block-scaled MMA and needs UE8M0 scales per row and 32 columns, so the routed and shared expert weights are requantized once at load (`requant_block_fp8_to_ue8m0`).
- This requantization is lossy: about 2.4% relative L2 per weight tensor and about 3.9% on one MoE layer's output (layer 15, real weights, random inputs). The generic TRTLLM path uses the checkpoint's scales as they are. The GSM8K gap above is within one standard error.
- Routing stays outside the kernel: `fused_topk_bias` (sigmoid, score correction bias), with `routed_scaling_factor` folded into the top-k weights. DeepGEMM's Mega Gate only supports `sqrtsoftplus`.
- `Glm5NextMegaMoEExperts` subclasses `DeepGemmMegaMoEExperts`, which is unchanged, with the `MEGA_MOE_MXFP8` format. E4M3 shards load straight into the kernel layout; their float32 block scales are staged in `*_weight_scale_inv`, and the model's `process_weights_after_loading` calls `requantize_block_fp8()`, which rounds every newly loaded shard to UE8M0 1x32 scales in place (main model, multimodal wrapper and MTP drafter).
- A weight update may send an expert weight and its block scale in separate `load_weights` calls; by the end of the load both must be in, or `requantize_block_fp8()` raises.
- Reload and weight transfer finish with that hook (#64357, and direct mode from #64336), so the kernel tensors keep their storage. The derived UE8M0 scales are marked `weight_loader_numel = 0`, so a layerwise reload replays a layer as soon as its checkpoint tensors are in.
- The block-FP8 shared expert is fused the same way: the experts own its weights and the model builds no shared MLP.
- `--prefix-match-unit` matters for this model independently of this PR: the KDA state page makes the KV block 8,960 tokens under DEP4, and without the flag prefix hits land on whole blocks.
- Limitations: `tensor_parallel_size=1` only; SM100 only; no sharded RDT or sparse NCCL updates. Under DEP4 each rank holds 8.8M KV tokens.

Some independent data on the accuracy question, from the full **GLM-5.3** (FP8 checkpoint) rather than the Flash model.

We run a prototype of the same approach for GLM-5.3's routed experts: DeepGEMM FP8xFP8 MegaMoE, block-FP8 weights requantized to UE8M0 1x32 with the same rounding as this PR, shared expert outside the kernel. GLM-5.3 goes through `DeepseekV2MoE`, so the prototype hooks in there. It ran on one 8x B300 node with prefill context parallelism (PCP8, TP1, EP8), MTP 1, FP8 KV cache, on vLLM v0.31.0. Same pod and identical prompts for both arms; the only difference is the MoE (FlashInfer TRT-LLM on the checkpoint's own scales vs MegaMoE):

| | FlashInfer TRT-LLM | MegaMoE |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K, 1,319 questions, greedy, chat (reasoning effort low) | 96.36% | 96.59% |
| Long-context retrieval, code at 5 depths, 32k / 64k / 128k / 187k tokens | 20/20 | 20/20 |
| Cold prefill, 16k prompts, 8 in flight | 54.0k tok/s | 85.8k tok/s (+59%) |
| Cold prefill, 16k prompts, 24 in flight | 55.9k tok/s | 90.8k tok/s (+62%) |

- GSM8K: 7 questions right only with TRT-LLM, 10 only with MegaMoE (McNemar p = 0.63); 98.3% have the same final answer.
- So on the large model we see no GSM8K regression from the UE8M0 requantization either. This is a narrow check, not AIME or AA-LCR.

Two things we had to handle that this PR doesn't cover yet, in case they're useful for a follow-up:

1. **`DeepseekV2MoE` models** (GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V3.2): routing is sigmoid + `e_score_correction_bias`, renormalized, times `routed_scaling_factor`, computed outside the kernel; the shared expert runs separately.
2. **Prefill context parallelism**: MegaMoE is a collective over the EP group, so every rank must call it the same number of times per layer. With PCP every rank has the same padded token count, so splitting large batches into fixed-size chunks (we use 8192 tokens per rank per call) keeps the call counts equal.

Once this lands, I'd be happy to open a follow-up that wires the `deep_gemm_mega_moe` backend into `DeepseekV2MoE`, with PCP support, and run the same checks on B300.

Follow-up for the full GLM-5.x / DeepSeek-V3.2 (`DeepseekV2MoE`, DSA models), stacked on this PR: #63119 (draft). It reuses `Glm5NextMegaMoEExperts` as is, keeps the shared expert as a separate MLP, and works with data parallel and prefill context parallel. I'll rebase it once this lands.

detail.body:
## Overview

Run GLM-5.3-Flash's MoE layers with DeepGEMM's FP8xFP8 MegaMoE (routed and shared experts in one kernel that also dispatches and combines across the EP group), using the official FP8 checkpoint. Enabled by `--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'` with `--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size N --enable-expert-parallel`.

Related: #55275 (BF16 / MXFP4 MegaMoE for GLM, open), #54049 (FlashInfer NVFP4 mega kernel).

## Claims

- On the AgentX replay at concurrency 96, DEP4 with MegaMoE gives 1.6x the output throughput of DEP4 on the generic MoE path.
- Against TP4 it is about level on throughput (+6%, one run each) and has about a fifth of the TTFT.
- It prefills 1.8x faster than DEP4 generic and 2.5x faster than TP4.
- AIME 2026 Pass@1 matches the generic MoE path (0.934 vs 0.939 with a 131K output cap) and is 0.977 with the 1M context.
- A weight reload, in layerwise or direct mode, restores byte-identical weights at the same addresses.
- No change for any other `moe_backend`.

## Validation

4x B200, nightly `8cbd5d03` with this change applied, MTP 5 with acceptance fixed by `synthetic_acceptance_length` 3.61. The three arms ran on the same node and in the same container, one run each; they differ only in parallel layout and `moe_backend`.

AgentX replay (InferenceX-pinned aiperf, `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126`), concurrency 96, 1 hour:

| metric | TP4 | DEP4, generic MoE | DEP4, MegaMoE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| output tok/s | 3,152 | 2,063 | **3,332** |
| input tok/s | 380,126 | 234,727 | **399,297** |
| total tok/s | 383,278 | 236,790 | **402,628** |
| requests completed (errors) | 11,372 (4) | 8,143 (1) | 11,986 (5) |
| TTFT avg / p50 / p99 | 3.93 / 2.19 / 23.8 s | 2.36 / 1.47 / 17.3 s | **0.81 / 0.49 / 5.99 s** |
| ITL avg | 18.3 ms | 45.6 ms | 19.5 ms |
| output tok/s per user | 64.0 | 26.2 | 64.1 |
| prefix cache hit | 93.9% | 92.4% | 94.0% |
| of which GPU / host reload | 6.2% / 87.7% | 50.9% / 41.5% | 71.2% / 22.8% |
| preemptions | 35 | 53 | 2 |

`vllm bench serve`, random prompts, concurrency 128, on the same servers:

| workload (in/out) | metric | TP4 | DEP4, generic MoE | DEP4, MegaMoE |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 / 1 | total tok/s | 46,334 | 63,900 | **115,081** |
| | mean TTFT | 20.8 s | 15.2 s | 8.4 s |
| 1024 / 1024 | output tok/s | 7,895 | 8,478 | **11,691** |
| | mean TTFT | 4.31 s | 1.86 s | 0.85 s |

Accuracy:

| eval | TP4 | DEP4, generic MoE | DEP4, MegaMoE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K, lm-eval 5-shot, 1,319 questions | 0.9757 ± 0.0042 | – | 0.9735 ± 0.0044 |
| AIME 2026 Pass@1, 30 problems x 32 samples | – | 0.939 ± 0.006 | 0.934 ± 0.006 |

GSM8K ran on nightly `43b4aaea` (TP4) and the servers above (MegaMoE). AIME ran on nightly `df3bd094` with this branch, both arms in the same container (MTP 3, fp8 KV, 131K output cap) with DeepInfer's `eval/aime` prompt and rule-based judge, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95; the generic arm runs `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` on the checkpoint's own scales. With the full 1M context MegaMoE reaches **0.977 ± 0.005**; the remaining loss is mostly problem 15 (0.72), where 12 of 32 samples never stop and loop until the context is full.

Weight reload, 4x B200, nightly `e0d00e4b8e` with this branch, DEP4, MTP 3. The experts are zeroed before each reload, which breaks every greedy output; all results are compared with the cold start:

| metric | layerwise | direct |
|---|---:|---:|
| target reload time | 41.6 s | 37.3 s |
| parameters and buffers differing (5,900 across ranks) | 0 | 0 |
| parameters and buffers moved | 0 | 0 |
| greedy outputs matching (4 short prompts) | 4/4 | 4/4 |

The same holds for a second reload, a reload of the MTP drafter, and an update that sends expert weights and block scales in separate `load_weights` calls. Long prompts (about 14K tokens) already vary between identical runs without a reload, on both MoE backends, so they are not compared. No real NCCL or IPC trainer was run.

Unit tests: `pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_mega_moe.py`, 5 passed.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 PYTHONHASHSEED=42 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.61}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true,"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[6,12,18,24,30,36,48,60,72,96,120,144,192,240,288,384,480,576,768,1020,1536,2046,3072,4092,6144,8190]}' \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 8190 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 \
  --prefix-match-unit 16 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":300000000000,"enable_cross_layers_blocks":"true","lazy_offload":false}}'

vllm-router --port 8000 --worker-urls http://127.0.0.1:8001 --intra-node-data-parallel-size 4 --policy consistent_hash

aiperf profile --scenario agentx --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --concurrency 96 --benchmark-duration 3600 \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126
```

AIME 2026:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92
```

The client sends DeepInfer's `eval/aime` prompts (`build_records`) to `/v1/chat/completions` with `temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95`, 32 samples per problem, and scores `reasoning + "</think>" + content` with its `score_rollout`. Samples were drawn with a 131K output cap first; the 82 that hit it were continued from their own text to the 1M context, which samples the same distribution as the larger cap.

The baselines drop `moe_backend` (DEP4, generic) or use `--tensor-parallel-size 4` alone with `--intra-node-data-parallel-size 1` on the router (TP4). The generic path picked `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` for the FP8 experts. The random-prompt rows were measured on the same servers before the replay with `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --max-concurrency 128`.
</details>

## Details

- The checkpoint's experts are block FP8 (E4M3, one float32 scale per 128x128 block). DeepGEMM's SM100 MegaMoE feeds scales to the block-scaled MMA and needs UE8M0 scales per row and 32 columns, so the routed and shared expert weights are requantized once at load (`requant_block_fp8_to_ue8m0`).
- This requantization is lossy: about 2.4% relative L2 per weight tensor and about 3.9% on one MoE layer's output (layer 15, real weights, random inputs). The generic TRTLLM path uses the checkpoint's scales as they are. The GSM8K gap above is within one standard error.
- Routing stays outside the kernel: `fused_topk_bias` (sigmoid, score correction bias), with `routed_scaling_factor` folded into the top-k weights. DeepGEMM's Mega Gate only supports `sqrtsoftplus`.
- `Glm5NextMegaMoEExperts` subclasses `DeepGemmMegaMoEExperts`, which is unchanged, with the `MEGA_MOE_MXFP8` format. E4M3 shards load straight into the kernel layout; their float32 block scales are staged in `*_weight_scale_inv`, and the model's `process_weights_after_loading` calls `requantize_block_fp8()`, which rounds every newly loaded shard to UE8M0 1x32 scales in place (main model, multimodal wrapper and MTP drafter).
- A weight update may send an expert weight and its block scale in separate `load_weights` calls; by the end of the load both must be in, or `requantize_block_fp8()` raises.
- Reload and weight transfer finish with that hook (#64357, and direct mode from #64336), so the kernel tensors keep their storage. The derived UE8M0 scales are marked `weight_loader_numel = 0`, so a layerwise reload replays a layer as soon as its checkpoint tensors are in.
- The block-FP8 shared expert is fused the same way: the experts own its weights and the model builds no shared MLP.
- `--prefix-match-unit` matters for this model independently of this PR: the KDA state page makes the KV block 8,960 tokens under DEP4, and without the flag prefix hits land on whole blocks.
- Limitations: `tensor_parallel_size=1` only; SM100 only; no sharded RDT or sparse NCCL updates. Under DEP4 each rank holds 8.8M KV tokens.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""GLM-5.3-Flash MegaMoE: block-FP8 checkpoint shards requantized to the
+MXFP8 MegaMoE kernel layout."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.deep_gemm_mega_moe import MegaMoEActivation
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp8_utils import (
+    requant_block_fp8_to_ue8m0,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload import (
+    finish_reload,
+    record_metadata_for_reloading,
+    start_reload,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.utils import process_weights_after_loading
+from vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia.mega_moe import Glm5NextMegaMoEExperts
+
+BLOCK = (128, 128)
+HIDDEN, INTER = 256, 128
+FP8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn
+NUM_EXPERTS = 4
+# Global ids of the experts _experts() places on this rank.
+LOCAL_EXPERTS = slice(2, 4)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def sm100_mega_moe_layout(monkeypatch):
+    """Build the SM100 kernel layout on any device."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        "vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.deep_gemm_mega_moe."
+        "check_deep_gemm_mega_moe_supported",
+        lambda *args: None,
+    )
+
+
+def _block_fp8(real: torch.Tensor, power_of_two: bool = False):
+    """Quantize ``(..., mn, k)`` to E4M3 with one float32 scale per 128x128."""
+    *lead, mn, k = real.shape
+    blocks = real.reshape(*lead, mn // 128, 128, k // 128, 128)
+    scale = blocks.abs().amax(dim=(-3, -1)) / 448.0
+    if power_of_two:
+        scale = torch.exp2(torch.ceil(torch.log2(scale)))
+    full = scale.repeat_interleave(128, -2).repeat_interleave(128, -1)
+    return (real / full).to(FP8), scale
+
+
+def _dequant_block(weight: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return weight.float() * scale.repeat_interleave(128, -2).repeat_interleave(128, -1)
+
+
+def _dequant_ue8m0(weight: torch.Tensor, sf: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return weight.float() * torch.exp2(sf.float() - 127).repeat_interleave(32, -1)
+
+
+def test_requant_is_exact_for_power_of_two_block_scales():
+    torch.manual_seed(1)
+    real = torch.randn(1, 256, 256) * 0.05
+    weight, scale = _block_fp8(real, power_of_two=True)
+
+    requant, sf = requant_block_fp8_to_ue8m0(weight, scale)
+
+    # A finer power-of-two scale only shifts exponents, so nothing rounds.
+    assert torch.equal(_dequant_ue8m0(requant, sf), _dequant_block(weight, scale))
+
+
+def _experts() -> Glm5NextMegaMoEExperts:
+    vllm_config = SimpleNamespace(
+        scheduler_config=SimpleNamespace(max_num_batched_tokens=64),
+        compilation_config=SimpleNamespace(static_forward_context={}),
+    )
+    return Glm5NextMegaMoEExperts(
+        vllm_config,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+        num_experts=NUM_EXPERTS,
+        num_local_experts=2,
+        experts_start_idx=2,
+        top_k=2,
+        hidden_size=HIDDEN,
+        intermediate_size=INTER,
+        weight_block_size=BLOCK,
+        activation=MegaMoEActivation("swiglu", clamp=10.0),
+        num_shared_experts=1,
+        prefix="model.layers.3.mlp.experts",
+    )
+
+
+def _checkpoint(seed: int) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Block-FP8 experts as stored: gate rows, then up rows, for w13."""
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+
+    def rand(*shape):
+        return torch.randn(*shape, generator=generator) * 0.02
+
+    w13, s13 = _block_fp8(rand(NUM_EXPERTS, 2 * INTER, HIDDEN))
+    w2, s2 = _block_fp8(rand(NUM_EXPERTS, HIDDEN, INTER))
+    return {
+        "w13_weight": w13,
+        "w13_weight_scale_inv": s13,
+        "w2_weight": w2,
+        "w2_weight_scale_inv": s2,
+    }
+
+
+def _load_shuffled(experts, ckpt, seed, suffix="") -> None:
+    """Load the checkpoint tensors whose names end in ``suffix``, shuffled."""
+    shards = []
+    for expert_id in range(NUM_EXPERTS):
+        for name, tensor in ckpt.items():
+            if not name.endswith(suffix):
+                continue
+            if name.startswith("w2_"):
+                shards.append((name, tensor[expert_id], "w2", expert_id))
+            else:
+                half = tensor.shape[1] // 2
+                shards.append((name, tensor[expert_id, :half], "w1", expert_id))
+                shards.append((name, tensor[expert_id, half:], "w3", expert_id))
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    for i in torch.randperm(len(shards), generator=generator).tolist():
+        name, loaded_weight, shard_id, expert_id = shards[i]
+        param = getattr(experts, name)
+        loaded = param.weight_loader(
+            param,
+            loaded_weight,
+            f"experts.{name}",
+            shard_id=shard_id,
+            expert_id=expert_id,
+            return_success=True,
+        )
+        # Physical experts 2 and 3 are this rank's.
+        assert loaded == (expert_id >= 2)
+
+
+def _reference_mega_moe_layout(w13, s13, w2, s2):
+    """CPU copy of DeepGEMM's transform_weights_for_mega_moe on packed scales."""
+
+    def interleave(t):
+        g, n, k = t.shape
+        halves = t.view(g, 2, n // 16, 8, k)
+        return torch.stack([halves[:, 0], halves[:, 1]], dim=2).reshape(g, n, k)
+
+    def utccp(sf):
+        g, mn, k = sf.shape
+        return sf.reshape(g, -1, 4, 32, k).transpose(2, 3).reshape(g, mn, k)
+
+    return (
+        interleave(w13.view(torch.uint8)),
+        utccp(interleave(s13.view(torch.int32))),
+        w2.view(torch.uint8),
+        utccp(s2.view(torch.int32)),
+    )
+
+
+def _expected_routed(ckpt):
+    w13, s13 = requant_block_fp8_to_ue8m0(
+        ckpt["w13_weight"][LOCAL_EXPERTS], ckpt["w13_weight_scale_inv"][LOCAL_EXPERTS]
+    )
+    w2, s2 = requant_block_fp8_to_ue8m0(
+        ckpt["w2_weight"][LOCAL_EXPERTS], ckpt["w2_weight_scale_inv"][LOCAL_EXPERTS]
+    )
+    return _reference_mega_moe_layout(w13, s13, w2, s2)
+
+
+def _assert_layout(actual, expected):
+    for tensor, reference in zip(actual, expected):
+        assert torch.equal(tensor.view(reference.dtype), reference)
+
+
+def _routed(experts):
+    return (*experts.l1_weights, *experts.l2_weights)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("first", ["weight", "weight_scale_inv"])
+def test_weight_update_split_across_calls(first):
+    """A weight update may send weights and block scales in separate
+    load_weights calls. The finish step rejects a shard still missing its
+    other half and requantizes each shard once both are in."""
+    experts = _experts()
+    _load_shuffled(experts, _checkpoint(seed=0), seed=0)
+    experts.requantize_block_fp8()
+
+    ckpt = _checkpoint(seed=1)
+    second = "weight_scale_inv" if first == "weight" else "weight"
+    _load_shuffled(experts, ckpt, seed=1, suffix=first)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="without their weight or block scale"):
+        experts.requantize_block_fp8()
+    _load_shuffled(experts, ckpt, seed=2, suffix=second)
+    experts.requantize_block_fp8()
+
+    _assert_layout(_routed(experts), _expected_routed(ckpt))
+
+
+def _shared_checkpoint(seed: int) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    w13, s13 = _block_fp8(torch.randn(1, 2 * INTER, HIDDEN, generator=generator) * 0.02)
+    w2, s2 = _block_fp8(torch.randn(1, HIDDEN, INTER, generator=generator) * 0.02)
+    return {"w13": w13, "s13": s13, "w2": w2, "s2": s2}
+
+
+def _load_shared(experts, ckpt) -> None:
+    w13, s13, w2, s2 = ckpt["w13"], ckpt["s13"], ckpt["w2"], ckpt["s2"]
+    params = {f"mlp.experts.{n}" for n, _ in experts.named_parameters()}
+    for name, data in [
+        ("down_proj.weight_scale_inv", s2[0]),
+        ("gate_proj.weight", w13[0, :INTER]),
+        ("up_proj.weight_scale_inv", s13[0, 1:]),
+        ("down_proj.weight", w2[0]),
+        ("up_proj.weight", w13[0, INTER:]),
+        ("gate_proj.weight_scale_inv", s13[0, :1]),

Some independent data on the accuracy question, from the full **GLM-5.3** (FP8 checkpoint) rather than the Flash model.

We run a prototype of the same approach for GLM-5.3's routed experts: DeepGEMM FP8xFP8 MegaMoE, block-FP8 weights requantized to UE8M0 1x32 with the same rounding as this PR, shared expert outside the kernel. GLM-5.3 goes through `DeepseekV2MoE`, so the prototype hooks in there. It ran on one 8x B300 node with prefill context parallelism (PCP8, TP1, EP8), MTP 1, FP8 KV cache, on vLLM v0.31.0. Same pod and identical prompts for both arms; the only difference is the MoE (FlashInfer TRT-LLM on the checkpoint's own scales vs MegaMoE):

| | FlashInfer TRT-LLM | MegaMoE |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K, 1,319 questions, greedy, chat (reasoning effort low) | 96.36% | 96.59% |
| Long-context retrieval, code at 5 depths, 32k / 64k / 128k / 187k tokens | 20/20 | 20/20 |
| Cold prefill, 16k prompts, 8 in flight | 54.0k tok/s | 85.8k tok/s (+59%) |
| Cold prefill, 16k prompts, 24 in flight | 55.9k tok/s | 90.8k tok/s (+62%) |

- GSM8K: 7 questions right only with TRT-LLM, 10 only with MegaMoE (McNemar p = 0.63); 98.3% have the same final answer.
- So on the large model we see no GSM8K regression from the UE8M0 requantization either. This is a narrow check, not AIME or AA-LCR.

Two things we had to handle that this PR doesn't cover yet, in case they're useful for a follow-up:

1. **`DeepseekV2MoE` models** (GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V3.2): routing is sigmoid + `e_score_correction_bias`, renormalized, times `routed_scaling_factor`, computed outside the kernel; the shared expert runs separately.
2. **Prefill context parallelism**: MegaMoE is a collective over the EP group, so every rank must call it the same number of times per layer. With PCP every rank has the same padded token count, so splitting large batches into fixed-size chunks (we use 8192 tokens per rank per call) keeps the call counts equal.

Once this lands, I'd be happy to open a follow-up that wires the `deep_gemm_mega_moe` backend into `DeepseekV2MoE`, with PCP support, and run the same checks on B300.
